title: Write the Finding (pentest report — Google Doc)
description:
Amaka: 'Pick one. The SQL injection or the SSRF. Write it up as a proper penetration test finding — not a summary, a structured finding that could go into a client-facing report. I need a technical lead who has never seen this application to understand exactly what happened, why it is dangerous, and what to do about it.'

**Submission via Google Doc link.** Pentest findings need tables (severity matrix, affected assets), code blocks (the payload, the curl reproduction), and headings — the writeup pad cannot render those. Write the finding in a Google Doc, set sharing to **'Anyone with the link → Viewer'** (we will not chase access requests), then paste the URL below along with a 50+ word abstract.

**Required structure in the Doc (in this order, with these section headings exactly):**

1. **Title** — single line, of the form `[VULN-CLASS] Component — One-line impact`.

2. **Severity** — Critical / High / Medium / Low. Justify with a CVSS v3.1 vector string (e.g. `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`) and the resulting base score. Use the FIRST CVSS calculator (https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1).

3. **Affected component** — service name, endpoint path, file path or function if you can identify one from the artefacts in this stage. If you cannot identify the function, name the layer (router / data access / template).

4. **Reproduction steps** — numbered, each step one short imperative sentence. Include the exact payload in a code block and a `curl` command that reproduces it. A grader should be able to follow your steps with no prior knowledge of the app.

5. **Impact** — a paragraph (60+ words) on what an attacker achieves and how far the impact reaches. Be specific about the data class (customer PII, credentials, transaction records, IAM tokens) and the blast radius (single user, all dashboard users, the entire cloud account).

6. **Root cause** — a paragraph on the code-or-design failure that allowed it. Not the symptom — the cause. Not "the input wasn't validated" — "the data access layer concatenated user input directly into SQL" or "the URL-fetching function trusted user-supplied destinations including link-local ranges with no allow-list".

7. **Recommended fix** — a paragraph. The fix that addresses the root cause, not the symptom. Include one sentence on what would **not** fix it (the seductive wrong answer — input sanitisation for SQL injection; character blocklisting for XSS; rate-limiting for SSRF).

8. **References** — OWASP entry by ID (`A03:2021 Injection`), CWE ID (`CWE-89` / `CWE-918`), and one MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (`T1190`). Quote them in full — "OWASP A03" alone loses 3 pts; `OWASP A03:2021 Injection — CWE-89 SQL Injection` passes.

9. **Evidence appendix** — the artefacts you read to support every claim above. Log lines (with file + timestamp), task numbers from this stage, payloads you sent in the VULN_APP_SIM. Any claim above not backed by an entry here loses 3 pts.

10. **One mistake I almost made** — 40+ words on a specific moment in this investigation where you nearly miswrote the finding (chose the wrong CWE; mislabeled the severity; conflated the search-field XSS with the notes-feature XSS).

**Minimum 400 words in the Doc.** Paste the link below plus a 50+ word abstract here in the pad so the grader knows what they are about to open.

Amaka signs these before they go to the client.

**Add section 11 — Retest plan (60+ words).** Describe how you would verify the fix took effect. List the exact requests / payloads / queries you would re-run, the negative result that proves the vulnerability is closed (status code, response body shape, log line absence), and one regression test you would add to CI so it cannot silently come back. A fix without a retest is a guess.

---

**Universal grading rule.** Generic answers fail. Every claim in your submission must be tied to specific evidence — an artefact from the lab (file path, log line, command output, payload, screenshot) **and** at least one external citation where research is relevant (NIST section number, MITRE technique ID, CVE, vendor advisory, ISO control ID, NDPA section). Claims without an attached artefact, timestamp, payload, standard section, or business constraint earn zero for that claim. Lab-only answers earn partial credit. External-only answers earn partial credit. Full credit requires both.
